review_candidates.title: Azure Specialist
review_candidates.description: Who We Are: TrustedTech is a leading Microsoft Cloud Solution Provider (CSP) specializing in Microsoft Cloud services, Microsoft perpetual licensing, and Microsoft Support Services for medium and enterprise-sized businesses. Our robust team of in-house, global Microsoft architects and engineers are certified in all 6/6 Microsoft Solutions Partner Designations in the Microsoft Cloud Partner Program. Prioritizing a people-centric mission, TrustedTech has transformed the Microsoft software licensing experience, giving IT professionals complete confidence in the success of their Microsoft investment. TrustedTech is the fastest-growing Microsoft Partner globally, with a presence in the UK and Europe for just over four years. Our continued success is built on relentless customer focus, innovation, and a world-class team. You’ll be joining a high-energy, high-impact organisation with the opportunity to make the role your own and directly influence our growth across the region. Overview: TrustedTech is seeking an experienced, bilingual Azure Support Specialist (German/English) to serve as a primary technical advisor within our EMEA Cloud Support team. This is a sophisticated, customer-facing role designed for an Azure expert who combines deep technical remediation with commercial acumen and a consultative approach, and who can engage German-speaking clients with fluency, credibility, and professionalism. The successful candidate will navigate complex cloud environments to resolve critical break/fix challenges while providing proactive, best-practice guidance aligned with Microsoft’s Well-Architected Framework and Cloud Adoption Framework. Acting in a consultative capacity, this person bridges the gap between technical complexity and business value, ensuring the architectural health, operational readiness, and long-term scalability of a diverse client portfolio across Germany and the broader EMEA region. This role also serves as an escalation point for complex issues and contributes meaningfully to the mentoring and technical development of the wider EMEA Cloud Engineering team. Responsibilities: Reactive Support (Break/Fix) & Incident Resolution: Own technical break/fix engagements for Azure resources, providing customers with clear, actionable remediation steps and follow-through to resolution — communicating fluently in both German and English as required. Troubleshoot across core Azure services (IaaS/PaaS), including compute, storage, networking, identity, monitoring, and virtual desktop workloads. Perform root cause analysis (RCA) and document incident learnings to reduce repeat issues and improve customer outcomes. Act as an escalation point for complex or high-priority technical issues within the EMEA support team, ensuring timely and effective resolution with appropriate communication throughout. Customer Advisory (Best Practice Guidance): Provide customer-facing advisory aligned to Microsoft best practices, helping German-speaking and broader EMEA clients improve architecture hygiene, operational readiness, and governance. Develop and support comprehensive Azure cloud strategies for clients, spanning IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS solutions tailored to their business objectives and growth trajectory. Run lightweight health checks and advisory reviews covering monitoring posture, backup and DR readiness, and security baseline alignment. Translate technical findings into executive-friendly summaries and pragmatic next steps, communicating clearly and confidently with both technical and non-technical stakeholders in German and English. Customer Engagement & Leadership: Serve as the technical lead during client engagements, representing TrustedTech’s expertise and professionalism across all customer-facing interactions within the German-speaking market and EMEA region. Mentor Cloud Engineers by delivering targeted Azure training that supports technical upskilling and professional development within the EMEA team. Identify and drive process improvement and standardisation opportunities across Azure and M365 delivery practices. Apply a strong understanding of security, compliance, and governance within M365, including Entra ID identity architecture, Conditional Access, MFA, and SSO. Cost Optimisation (FinOps) & Performance Efficiency: Identify and deliver opportunities to optimise Azure spend while maintaining or improving performance and resilience. Advise customers on cost controls and right-sizing, including workload scheduling, scaling approaches, and storage tiering. Where appropriate, support commitment-based optimisation approaches such as aligning Reservations and Savings Plans to predictable workloads, ensuring recommendations reflect real utilisation and do not create unnecessary exposure. Automation, DevOps & Continuous Improvement: Identify opportunities for automation to improve reliability, response times, and consistency across the EMEA support function. Implement and support DevOps practices where appropriate, including Infrastructure as Code (IaC), repeatable deployments, scripting, and standard runbooks. Drive process improvements by refining support workflows, templates, and knowledge articles based on real ticket patterns and recurring themes. Documentation, Reporting & Operational Rigour: Maintain accurate internal documentation relating to Azure subscriptions, customer environments, and support actions. Produce high-quality client-facing documentation and concise reports that clearly communicate issues, fixes, and recommendations — in German and/or English as appropriate for the client. Ensure all work is delivered in line with documented processes, SLAs, and quality standards. Collaboration & Solution Shaping: Collaborate with customers and internal teams to gather requirements and propose practical Azure hosting and operational solutions that align to business goals. Contribute to the planning, execution, and validation of cloud migrations, supporting cutover readiness and post-migration stabilisation. Support secure, scalable, and compliant Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) deployments, including operational readiness, ongoing optimisation, and adherence to scalability and security standards. Required Skills & Qualifications (must-haves): 3–5 years of hands-on Azure support and/or solution design experience across Azure IaaS/PaaS and core services, including Compute, Storage, Networking, Azure SQL, Monitoring, and AVD. Business-level fluency in both German and English, with the confidence and professionalism to deliver technical advisory and client-facing communications in either language. Strong troubleshooting capability across Azure networking (VNets, routing, private endpoints), security controls (NSGs, RBAC), resiliency concepts (Availability Zones/Sets), backup and DR (ASR), connectivity (VPN/ExpressRoute), and observability (Azure Monitor/Log Analytics). AZ-104: Azure Administrator Associate certification is required. Comfortable performing hands-on tasks in the Azure Portal and on Windows/Linux VMs, with confidence scripting and automating using PowerShell or equivalent. Experience contributing to cloud migration planning and delivery, including assessment, execution, and post-migration validation. Solid knowledge of Microsoft identity and access management, including Entra ID/Azure AD, Conditional Access, AAD Connect, and SSO/SAML. Practical experience implementing monitoring, scaling, cost controls, security, and governance in real client environments. Familiarity with the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework and its practical application in customer engagements. Strong client-facing communication skills, with the ability to present technical findings and recommendations clearly to both technical audiences and executive stakeholders. Preferred Skills & Qualifications (nice-to-haves): AZ-305: Designing Microsoft Azure Infrastructure Solutions or AZ-700: Azure Network Engineer Associate — either certification is strongly preferred and reflects the depth of expertise this role demands. Prior experience supporting clients within the German-speaking market (DACH region), with familiarity with the business culture, enterprise IT landscape, and client expectations common in that region. AVD administration and troubleshooting, including automation, scaling, image management (AIB/Packer), FSLogix configuration, and VDI migration exposure (Citrix/Horizon/RDS). Experience with Azure SQL variants (Managed Instance, SQL DB, SQL on VM) and/or PostgreSQL or Cosmos DB. Data platform exposure across Synapse Analytics, Databricks, or OneLake. Infrastructure as Code and DevOps experience using Terraform and/or ARM/Bicep, CI/CD pipelines, and Git-based workflows. Hands-on experience providing customer-facing cost optimisation recommendations, including tagging strategies, budgets and alerts, chargeback/showback inputs, and KPI reporting. CompTIA Network+ certification. *TrustedTech is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation/gender identity, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.*

review_candidates.title: Senior IT Support Engineer
review_candidates.description: 1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $400M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing. About 1Password At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work. If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future. The IT Support team helps employees get the technology they need to do their best work. As a Sr. IT Support Engineer, you’ll combine hands-on troubleshooting with artificial intelligence (AI), automation, and better support workflows to resolve complex issues and improve the employee technology experience. Your work will help make support faster, more reliable, and easier to use while reducing recurring problems across the organization. Reporting to the Team Lead, IT Support, this role is based in the United States and works with teams across multiple time zones. How We’re Using AI Today Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers. This is a remote opportunity within the US. What We're Looking For Bring 5+ years of experience in internal information technology (IT) support, workplace technology, IT operations, or a related field. Troubleshoot complex issues across identity and access, devices, software, software as a service (SaaS), and workplace applications. Use ticketing systems, knowledge bases, service catalogs, and support workflows to manage and improve employee support. Build or improve workflow automations using tools such as Console, Workato, Tines, or similar platforms. Apply AI tools to investigate issues, create knowledge, improve support, or automate routine work while recognizing when human review is needed. Use support metrics such as resolution quality, time to resolution, repeat demand, self-service completion, and employee feedback to evaluate improvements. Communicate technical issues clearly, collaborate effectively across teams, and provide thoughtful support during sensitive or ambiguous situations. Bonus Points For Experience with basic scripting, application programming interfaces (APIs), or technical integrations. Experience with identity and access management, endpoint management, or service-management administration. Experience supporting distributed teams across multiple time zones. review_candidates.description: About Remote Remote is solving modern organizations’ biggest challenge – navigating global employment compliantly with ease. We make it possible for businesses of all sizes to recruit, pay, and manage international teams. With our core values at heart and future focused work culture, our team works tirelessly on ambitious problems, asynchronously, around the world. You can find Remoters working from 6 different continents (Antarctica left to go!) and all of our positions are fully remote. With Innovation as one of the core values, we have built Automation and AI capabilities into the requirements for every role. We encourage every member of the Remote team to bring their talents, experiences and culture to the table to help us build the best-in-class HR platform. If you are energetic, curious, motivated and ambitious, be part of our world. Apply now and define the future of work! What this job can offer you As a critical extension of our clients’ HR teams, we navigate and advise on the intricate paths of global employment with unmatched speed, expertise, and precision. The vision of the Lifecycle team at Remote is not just about maintaining the gold standard in HR practices; it’s about elevating it, integrating cutting-edge technology solutions, and enriching customer experiences in over 80+ countries. On this team, your work directly influences our ability to sustain and extend our compliance coverage, continuously enhance our customer journeys, and significantly increase our operational capacity. You’re not just part of a team; you’re at the forefront of shaping the future of work, ensuring every interaction is fast, intuitive, and profoundly impactful. Dive into a role where your passion for innovation, commitment to excellence, and drive to make a global difference aligns with our mission to empower organizations worldwide to employ anyone, anywhere — compliantly. The Lifecycle Specialist, Employee Relations & Transitions manages employee exits for Remote's external employees with a focus on legal compliance and providing delightful customer service. Additionally, the specialist provides first-level Employee Relations support, guiding clients through workplace concerns and coordinating appropriate resources when needed. As part of a larger employee Lifecycle team, the Specialist is also expected to contribute to process improvements and initiatives in line with Remote's strategic goals and values. Key Responsibilities Offboarding Manage and resolve end-to-end employee exits across multiple international jurisdictions, prioritizing a superior offboarding experience for Remote's clients and their employees. Provide sound guidance and manage clients' requests on various HR matters, including but not limited to termination, resignation and transfer procedures, employment contracts, and redundancy processes, ensuring legal compliance and best practices. Lead and facilitate meetings with clients and external employees, including but not limited to workforce reduction consultation meetings, administrative hearings, negotiations in separations and settlements, providing guidance on terminations, and delivering termination outcomes. Influence and negotiate positive outcomes in complex terminations, balancing multiple stakeholders with competing interests. Liaise with and coordinate various internal and external stakeholders to ensure compliance in offboarding activities and audits, including but not limited to payroll, legal counsel, government bodies, and trade unions. Draft, tailor and administer all termination and supplementary documents with accuracy and attention to detail, ensuring employee records are maintained with strict adherence to privacy and confidentiality regulations. Process offboarding on Remote's internal HRIS platform, collaborating with various internal stakeholders, such as Customer Success, Legal, Payroll, Benefits, Time and Attendance, amongst other verticals, to ensure all aspects of the employee exit are administered correctly and promptly. Be the subject-matter expert and respond to internal and external queries on all offboarding matters in conjunction with Lifecycle's internal stakeholders. Navigate clients through Remote's Employee Relations resources and guides, helping them understand applicable policies and processes. Conduct preliminary assessment of workplace concerns, identifying key facts and applicable local regulations. Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to ensure appropriate handling of employee relations matters. Support clients in understanding progressive disciplinary approaches and documentation requirements. Monitor ongoing employee relations cases, ensuring timely follow-up and coordination with relevant stakeholders. Actively identify opportunities for and contribute to process improvements, automation, product development and overall customer and employee experience through the offboarding and employee relations processes. Key Requirements and Charactristics Experience as a HR Advisor or HR Business Partner, with generalist HR competencies and exposure across the employee lifecycle. Proven experience with a strong background in managing voluntary and involuntary exits (terminations) with care, sensitivity and legal compliance; and providing comprehensive HR support and guidance on employment laws and regulations, spanning various jurisdictions. Ability to interpret and apply industrial instruments, analyze complex HR issues, undertake research, provide practical solutions and effectively communicate recommendations to clients and internal stakeholders when operating in ambiguous and unfamiliar environments. Basic understanding of employee relations principles, progressive discipline approaches, and workplace investigation fundamentals. Excellent communication, influencing, conflict management, and negotiation skills, with the ability to confidently lead difficult conversations to a positive outcome, often where parties have conflicting interests, maintaining professionalism and strict confidentiality. Business-level (advanced) proficiency in written and spoken English, with additional languages considered a plus. Aptitude and appetite to innovate and optimize processes, continuously identifying and implementing opportunities for automation and championing best practices. Efficiency in operations, with an awareness of the importance of thorough record-keeping and data integrity. Tech-savvy, with the ability to successfully collaborate asynchronously on various tools, and adapt to new and evolving systems. Ability to work autonomously and cohesively in an international team in a fast-paced, asynchronous, remote environment with multiple priorities. Willingness to work flexible hours as needed. Proactive and self-motivated with a strong sense of ownership and accountability. Demonstrates strong automation and AI capabilities and AI fluency. We hope to inspire other companies to support global talent-hiring and bring local wealth to developing countries. At first glance our salary bands seem quite wide - here is some context. At Remote we have international operations and a globally distributed workforce. We use geo ranges to consider geographic pay differentials as part of our global compensation strategy to remain competitive in various markets while we hiring globally. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level and location, and our job titles may span more than one career level. The actual base pay for the successful candidate in this role is dependent upon many factors such as location, transferable or job-related skills, work experience, relevant training, business needs, and market demands. The base salary range may be subject to change. At Remote, we foster internal mobility as a key element of our culture of employee growth and development, supported by a compensation philosophy that guarantees pay equity and fairness. Therefore, all compensation changes associated with an internal move will be reviewed by the Total Rewards & People Enablement team on a case by case basis. The annual salary range for this full-time position is $46,500—$104,650 USD Benefits Our full benefits & perks are explained in our handbook at remote.com/r/benefits. As a global company, each country works differently, but some benefits/perks are for all Remoters: work from anywhere flexible paid time off flexible working hours (we are async) 16 weeks paid parental leave budget towards co-working spaces, learning and wellness (including gym memberships) mental health support services stock options home office budget & IT equipment How You’ll Plan Your Day (and Life) We work async at Remote which means you can plan your schedule around your life (and not around meetings). Read more at remote.com/async. You will be empowered to take ownership and be proactive. When in doubt you will default to action instead of waiting. Your life-work balance is important and you will be encouraged to put yourself and your family first, and fit work around your needs. If that sounds like something you want, apply now! How To Apply Please fill out the form below and upload your CV with a PDF format. We kindly ask you to submit your application and CV in English, as this is the standardised language we use here at Remote. If you don’t have an up to date CV but you are still interested in talking to us, please feel free to add a copy of your LinkedIn profile instead. Not only do we encourage folks from all ethnic groups, genders, sexuality, age, abilities, disability status and any other under-represented group to apply, but we prioritize a sense of belonging. During your interviews and beyond, we ask & encourage anybody who needs an accommodation to request one from their recruiter. We will ask you to voluntarily tell us your pronouns at interview stage, and you will have the option to answer our anonymous demographic questionnaire when you apply below. As an equal employment opportunity employer it’s important to us that our workforce reflects people of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences and this data will help us to stay accountable. We thank you for providing this data, if you chose to. At Remote, we embrace AI as a valuable tool while prioritizing human creativity and authenticity. We make it possible for businesses of all sizes to recruit, pay, and manage international teams. With our core values at heart and future focused work culture, our team works tirelessly on ambitious problems, asynchronously, around the world. You can find Remoters working from 6 different continents (Antarctica left to go!) and all of our positions are fully remote. With Innovation as one of the core values, we have built Automation and AI capabilities into the requirements for every role. We encourage every member of the Remote team to bring their talents, experiences and culture to the table to help us build the best-in-class HR platform. If you are energetic, curious, motivated and ambitious, be part of our world. Apply now and define the future of work! What this job can offer you As a critical extension of our clients’ HR teams, we navigate and advise on the intricate paths of global employment with unmatched speed, expertise, and precision. The vision of the Lifecycle team at Remote is not just about maintaining the gold standard in HR practices; it’s about elevating it, integrating cutting-edge technology solutions, and enriching customer experiences in over 80+ countries. On this team, your work directly influences our ability to sustain and extend our compliance coverage, continuously enhance our customer journeys, and significantly increase our operational capacity. You’re not just part of a team; you’re at the forefront of shaping the future of work, ensuring every interaction is fast, intuitive, and profoundly impactful. Dive into a role where your passion for innovation, commitment to excellence, and drive to make a global difference aligns with our mission to empower organizations worldwide to employ anyone, anywhere — compliantly. The Lifecycle Specialist, Employee Relations & Transitions manages employee exits for Remote's external employees with a focus on legal compliance and providing delightful customer service. Additionally, the specialist provides first-level Employee Relations support, guiding clients through workplace concerns and coordinating appropriate resources when needed. As part of a larger employee Lifecycle team, the Specialist is also expected to contribute to process improvements and initiatives in line with Remote's strategic goals and values. Key Responsibilities Offboarding Manage and resolve end-to-end employee exits across multiple international jurisdictions, prioritizing a superior offboarding experience for Remote's clients and their employees. Provide sound guidance and manage clients' requests on various HR matters, including but not limited to termination, resignation and transfer procedures, employment contracts, and redundancy processes, ensuring legal compliance and best practices. Lead and facilitate meetings with clients and external employees, including but not limited to workforce reduction consultation meetings, administrative hearings, negotiations in separations and settlements, providing guidance on terminations, and delivering termination outcomes. Influence and negotiate positive outcomes in complex terminations, balancing multiple stakeholders with competing interests. Liaise with and coordinate various internal and external stakeholders to ensure compliance in offboarding activities and audits, including but not limited to payroll, legal counsel, government bodies, and trade unions. Draft, tailor and administer all termination and supplementary documents with accuracy and attention to detail, ensuring employee records are maintained with strict adherence to privacy and confidentiality regulations. Process offboarding on Remote's internal HRIS platform, collaborating with various internal stakeholders, such as Customer Success, Legal, Payroll, Benefits, Time and Attendance, amongst other verticals, to ensure all aspects of the employee exit are administered correctly and promptly. Be the subject-matter expert and respond to internal and external queries on all offboarding matters in conjunction with Lifecycle's internal stakeholders. Navigate clients through Remote's Employee Relations resources and guides, helping them understand applicable policies and processes. Conduct preliminary assessment of workplace concerns, identifying key facts and applicable local regulations. Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to ensure appropriate handling of employee relations matters. Support clients in understanding progressive disciplinary approaches and documentation requirements. Monitor ongoing employee relations cases, ensuring timely follow-up and coordination with relevant stakeholders. Actively identify opportunities for and contribute to process improvements, automation, product development and overall customer and employee experience through the offboarding and employee relations processes. Key Requirements and Charactristics Experience as a HR Advisor or HR Business Partner, with generalist HR competencies and exposure across the employee lifecycle. Proven experience with a strong background in managing voluntary and involuntary exits (terminations) with care, sensitivity and legal compliance; and providing comprehensive HR support and guidance on employment laws and regulations, spanning various jurisdictions. Ability to interpret and apply industrial instruments, analyze complex HR issues, undertake research, provide practical solutions and effectively communicate recommendations to clients and internal stakeholders when operating in ambiguous and unfamiliar environments. Basic understanding of employee relations principles, progressive discipline approaches, and workplace investigation fundamentals. Excellent communication, influencing, conflict management, and negotiation skills, with the ability to confidently lead difficult conversations to a positive outcome, often where parties have conflicting interests, maintaining professionalism and strict confidentiality. Business-level (advanced) proficiency in written and spoken English, with additional languages considered a plus. Aptitude and appetite to innovate and optimize processes, continuously identifying and implementing opportunities for automation and championing best practices. Efficiency in operations, with an awareness of the importance of thorough record-keeping and data integrity. Tech-savvy, with the ability to successfully collaborate asynchronously on various tools, and adapt to new and evolving systems. Ability to work autonomously and cohesively in an international team in a fast-paced, asynchronous, remote environment with multiple priorities. Willingness to work flexible hours as needed. Proactive and self-motivated with a strong sense of ownership and accountability. Demonstrates strong automation and AI capabilities and AI fluency. Practicals You'll report to: Manager Employee Lifecycle, Employee Relations & Transitions Team: Lifecycle, Employee Relations & Transitions Location: EMEA Application process Interview with recruiter Take Home Exercise Interview with future manager Interview with team members (no managers present) Interview with Senior Manager Bar Raiser Prior employment verification check Remote's Total Rewards philosophy is to ensure fair, unbiased compensation and fair equity pay along with competitive benefits in all locations in which we operate. We do not agree to or encourage cheap-labor practices and therefore we ensure to pay above in-location rates. We hope to inspire other companies to support global talent-hiring and bring local wealth to developing countries. At first glance our salary bands seem quite wide - here is some context. At Remote we have international operations and a globally distributed workforce. We use geo ranges to consider geographic pay differentials as part of our global compensation strategy to remain competitive in various markets while we hiring globally. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level and location, and our job titles may span more than one career level. The actual base pay for the successful candidate in this role is dependent upon many factors such as location, transferable or job-related skills, work experience, relevant training, business needs, and market demands. The base salary range may be subject to change. At Remote, we foster internal mobility as a key element of our culture of employee growth and development, supported by a compensation philosophy that guarantees pay equity and fairness. Therefore, all compensation changes associated with an internal move will be reviewed by the Total Rewards & People Enablement team on a case by case basis. The annual salary range for this full-time position is $46,500—$104,650 USD Benefits Our full benefits & perks are explained in our handbook at remote.com/r/benefits. As a global company, each country works differently, but some benefits/perks are for all Remoters: work from anywhere flexible paid time off flexible working hours (we are async) 16 weeks paid parental leave budget towards co-working spaces, learning and wellness (including gym memberships) mental health support services stock options home office budget & IT equipment How You’ll Plan Your Day (and Life) We work async at Remote which means you can plan your schedule around your life (and not around meetings). Read more at remote.com/async. You will be empowered to take ownership and be proactive. When in doubt you will default to action instead of waiting. Your life-work balance is important and you will be encouraged to put yourself and your family first, and fit work around your needs. If that sounds like something you want, apply now! How To Apply Please fill out the form below and upload your CV with a PDF format. We kindly ask you to submit your application and CV in English, as this is the standardised language we use here at Remote. If you don’t have an up to date CV but you are still interested in talking to us, please feel free to add a copy of your LinkedIn profile instead. Not only do we encourage folks from all ethnic groups, genders, sexuality, age, abilities, disability status and any other under-represented group to apply, but we prioritize a sense of belonging. We have 4 ERGs (Women, Disability, Queer, Minorities in Tech) who meet regularly with the People team. During your interviews and beyond, we ask & encourage anybody who needs an accommodation to request one from their recruiter. We will ask you to voluntarily tell us your pronouns at interview stage, and you will have the option to answer our anonymous demographic questionnaire when you apply below. As an equal employment opportunity employer it’s important to us that our workforce reflects people of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences and this data will help us to stay accountable. We thank you for providing this data, if you chose to. At Remote, we embrace AI as a valuable tool while prioritizing human creativity and authenticity. We look forward to meeting candidates who balance innovation with genuine expertise and experience. To learn more about Remote's AI guidelines check see here. Please note we accept applications on an ongoing basis.

review_candidates.title: Executive Assistant to the SVP, Product Quality & Innovation
review_candidates.description: The opportunity Are you an accomplished Executive Assistant who thrives on building trusted relationships, anticipating what leaders need, and creating clarity in a complex international environment? We are looking for a Executive Assistant to partner with our Senior Vice President of Product Quality & Innovation. This is an influential role for someone who combines exceptional executive support with sound judgment, proactive communication, and a genuinely collaborative approach. You will serve as a trusted extension of the SVP, helping connect priorities, people, and information across an international leadership network. You will also join an experienced EA community where colleagues support one another, exchange best practices, and work together to make the wider organization more effective. What You Will Do Build a trusted, highly effective working partnership with the SVP, understanding priorities and anticipating needs. Create the planning, preparation, and structure that allow the SVP to focus on the most important business priorities. Manage a complex international calendar, travel arrangements, meeting preparation, correspondence, expenses, and other executive-level administration. Establish strong relationships across the leadership and EA community, acting as a reliable connection point between the SVP and key stakeholders. Anticipate upcoming meetings and decisions, ensuring that the right stakeholders are engaged and the necessary information is available in advance. Coordinate executive meetings, leadership events, and off-sites, ensuring a seamless experience from planning through execution. Communicate with professionalism, discretion, and good judgment on behalf of the SVP. Work within established company processes and help simplify and continuously improve ways of working. Contribute to an inclusive and collaborative EA community through knowledge sharing, coordination, and peer support. Support selected communications or cross-functional initiatives based on business needs and your individual strengths. What Will Help You Succeed Significant experience supporting a senior executive in a complex, international organization. Exceptional planning, organization, and prioritization skills. A proactive mindset and the ability to anticipate needs before they become urgent. Strong stakeholder-management skills and the confidence to work with senior leaders across functions and geographies. Excellent written and verbal communication. Sound judgment and the ability to handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion. A collaborative, service-oriented approach that builds trust and makes it easy for others to engage. High attention to detail and a strong commitment to following established policies and processes. Adaptability and composure when priorities change. Confidence using Microsoft Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and related collaboration tools. Availability for occasional domestic and international travel. Helpful, But Not Essential Previous experience supporting a C-suite executive or company president. Experience coordinating leadership events, off-sites, or executive programs. Interest or experience in internal communications, special projects, or EA-community development. Familiarity with continuous-improvement principles. Formal project-management experience. What Makes This Role Different This is more than a role that manages an executive’s schedule. It is an opportunity to build a close partnership with a senior leader, work across an international stakeholder community, and help improve the flow of information and collaboration across Product Quality & Innovation. The successful candidate will have the freedom to bring ideas, improve how work gets done, and expand their contribution over time through areas such as leadership events, communications, special initiatives, or EA-community development. At Veralto, we value diversity and the existence of similarities and differences, both visible and not, found in our workforce, workplace and throughout the markets we serve. Our associates, customers and shareholders contribute unique and different perspectives as a result of these diverse attributes. Unsolicited Assistance We do not accept unsolicited assistance from any headhunters or recruitment firms for any of our job openings. All resumes or profiles submitted by search firms to any employee at any of the Veralto companies, in any form without a valid, signed search agreement in place for the specific position, approved by Talent Acquisition, will be deemed the sole property of Veralto and its companies. No fee will be paid in the event the candidate is hired by Veralto and its companies because of the unsolicited referral.

We’re growing rapidly and looking for exceptional people to join us! About the Role Persona is excited to hire a Tech Ops Analyst to join our team! This position is perfect for individuals who are eager to build on their IT career in a high-growth technology startup environment. This role is ideal for individuals who are beginners in the field of IT but possess a strong passion for problem-solving and meticulous attention to detail, along with customer experience skills dealing with leaders as well as individual contributors. This step is used solely to confirm that candidates are who they say they are, and will have no impact on hiring decisions.

Support quality assurance by identifying defect trends and driving corrective actions. Support daily governance through country inputs, action tracking, and disciplined follow-through. Support audit readiness by maintaining complete, traceable, and current documentation. Enable change readiness through impact support, documentation updates, and training coordination. Drive continuous improvement by surfacing pain points and supporting simplification actions. Maintain country logs to ensure consistent guidance, stronger knowledge retention, and less ambiguity. Essential Requirements Strong knowledge of country HR processes, statutory requirements, and service expectations across supported Central European countries. Experience maintaining process documents, work instructions, and training materials in governance or outsourced environments. Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret data, identify themes, and draw practical conclusions. Experience in quality assurance, defect analysis, root cause identification, and corrective actions. Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills across vendors, markets, and internal governance teams. Ability to work within governance frameworks with sound judgment in issue triage, documentation, and escalation. Strong written communication skills for clear, structured, and audit-ready documentation. High personal accountability, strong attention to detail, and consistent follow-through. Proficiency in relevant market languages as required (Polish/ Romanian) Desirable Requirements 5+ years in HR services, shared services, outsourcing support, or operational excellence across Hire to Retire. Strong experience of leveraging SNOW for driving daily operational rigor demonstrated ability to streamline processes and support team members on scale-up Exposure to quality frameworks, governance models, or compliance-driven service delivery environments. Benefits & Rewards At Novartis, we’re committed to reimagining medicine together - and rewarding the people who make it happen. Expected Annual Base Salary Range for role: CZK 577 920 to CZK 1 073 280 The base salary offered is determined based on gender-neutral objectives, such as relevant skills, competencies and experience in accordance with the Novartis pay setting policy and upon joining Novartis will be reviewed periodically. In addition to your base salary, you may be eligible for a performance-based bonus depending on certain performance parameters. The rewards of being part of our team go far beyond base pay and incentives. We also offer a variety of competitive benefits in kind to help you thrive personally and professionally, such as insurance plans, retirement plans, wellbeing resources and global recognition programs. review_candidates.title: Junior Support Engineer
review_candidates.description: Junior Support Engineer 📍 Remote (Latin America-based; English-fluent) About the Company: Tricura Insurance Group is a next-generation, tech-enabled insurance and risk management company transforming how healthcare organizations protect, manage, and grow their operations. We're a global, remote-first team with headquarters in New York, reshaping the future of healthcare insurance. By combining deep industry expertise with modern technology, we deliver smarter, faster, and more transparent insurance solutions across the continuum of care. If you're motivated by impact, innovation, and purpose, you'll find your place here. About the Role: Tricura builds software for long-term-care and senior-living operators, turning clinical data from facility EHR systems into real-time alerts, compliance checks, and analytics. Our customers run dozens of facilities each, and the data behind every alert arrives through integrations we build and operate ourselves. Two things gate how fast we grow: how quickly we bring a new customer's data online, and how quickly we answer when something looks wrong. Both currently land on senior engineers as interrupts. This role exists to own those workflows properly and give the engineering team room to focus on deeper product and technical work. You're the first engineer on every incoming issue and every new customer connection. You diagnose before you escalate, run the onboarding sequence end to end, and write down how all of it works. Most customer issues reach engineering through our Customer Success team. You'll work closely with CS to understand what the customer is experiencing, investigate what is actually happening, and provide a clear technical answer or next step. CS owns the customer communication; you own the technical investigation, resolution, and handoff. This is an entry-level engineering role with a strong technical operations and support component. Some days you'll investigate an interesting production issue; other days you'll work through a detailed onboarding checklist or follow up on a missing access credential. The ability to approach both with the same level of care is central to succeeding in the role. What You'll Do: First response and triage. Reproduce incoming issues and classify them: genuine defect, expected behavior, data or config problem, or a question that needs a clear explanation rather than a fix. Resolve what you can, escalate well. Own straightforward issues to closure. When something needs a senior engineer, hand it over with the reproduction, the logs and queries, and the diagnosis already narrowed — never a forwarded complaint. Use good judgment about when to stop investigating. Your job is to identify the problem, gather enough evidence to establish what is happening, and escalate deeper issues effectively — not to disappear down a multi-day engineering rabbit hole. Work closely with Customer Success. CS is typically the channel through which customer feedback reaches engineering. You'll turn incomplete or sometimes ambiguous reports into actionable technical investigations and give CS the information they need to respond back to the customer. Run customer onboarding operations. Drive new orgs and facilities from intake through provisioning: the access and credential sequence with each customer's EHR vendor, configuration in our platform, and verification that data is actually flowing before anyone calls it live. Manage the onboarding checklist end to end. Work through the required technical steps, identify what information or access is missing or incorrect, and coordinate the follow-up needed to get onboarding unstuck. Keep the pipeline visible. Every in-flight onboarding tracked with its real blocker and its real owner, in the issue tracker rather than in chat history. Investigate data and configuration issues. Use the available platform data, queries, logs, and source-system information to determine whether an issue originates in incoming data, configuration, or the application itself. Follow established technical procedures. Existing onboarding and support workflows are documented and intentionally step-by-step. You'll learn them, execute them consistently, and gradually become able to run them independently. Write the playbooks. Every recurring procedure becomes a runbook: the steps, the failure modes, what to check, when to escalate. This is the lasting output of the role, not an afterthought. Turn tribal knowledge into documentation. When you learn how to solve a recurring problem that currently lives in someone's head, capture it so another person can follow the same process without needing to ask. Follow QA-quality bug reporting standards. Reproduction steps, evidence, and issue descriptions should be consistent with the standards used by the QA team so that engineering receives actionable bugs. Ship small fixes. Config corrections, data-quality queries, verification scripts, well-scoped bug fixes, reviewed like any other change. Who We're Looking For: 0–2 years of professional software experience , and a strong Computer Science / Engineering degree with real project work . We'll teach the domain; we won't teach how to think about a problem. Python and SQL. Read an unfamiliar Python codebase and follow what it does. Write SQL well enough to answer "is this customer's data actually correct?" unaided. Systematic debugging. Hypothesis, test, and the difference between a symptom and a cause. Comfortable saying "I reproduced it and here's why it happens." Strong signal-vs-noise judgment. You can distinguish a genuine defect from expected behavior, a configuration issue, bad or missing data, or a misunderstanding — and you don't automatically turn every customer complaint into a bug. Professional English fluency. Most of the job is written — triage notes, escalations, runbooks, status updates read by US-based colleagues. Clear communication. You can take a messy or incomplete problem statement and turn it into a structured explanation of what you know, what you tested, what remains unclear, and what needs to happen next. Comfort with ambiguity and process work. Some days are a genuinely interesting bug. Some days are chasing an access request through three parties. The role needs someone who treats the second with the same care as the first. Comfort learning from others. This is a junior role in a technically complex environment. You won't know everything, and that's expected. We value someone who can say "I don't know yet," ask a good question, and then learn from the answer. Attention to detail. Small differences in credentials, facility information, configuration, or incoming data can determine whether an onboarding succeeds. Ownership and follow-through. You don't need someone constantly reminding you which onboarding step is blocked or which investigation still needs an answer. Availability to work from 9 am to 6 pm EST . Strong Plus: Internship, university, side-project, open-source, or other hands-on experience where you've actually built or debugged software. Experience working with technical support, QA, incident triage, NOC, or production operations. Experience investigating issues in software you didn't originally build. Experience working with databases and using SQL to validate whether data is correct. Experience creating technical documentation, runbooks, READMEs, troubleshooting guides, or similar materials that other people could follow. Experience working with healthcare, long-term care, senior living, EHR systems, or other regulated environments with real privacy constraints. Experience with AWS, Airflow-style or similar workflow orchestration, cloud data platforms, warehouses, or related infrastructure. What Success Looks Like: In the first months, you'll learn the onboarding and support workflows, become comfortable navigating the relevant systems, and begin handling routine cases with guidance. Over time, you'll be able to independently: Triage incoming issues and quickly determine whether they are bugs, configuration/data issues, expected behavior, or misunderstandings. Reproduce and document problems clearly enough for engineering or QA to act on them. Resolve routine support and configuration issues without pulling senior engineers into the work. Run customer onboarding through the required technical steps and identify exactly what is blocking progress. Keep onboarding status and ownership visible rather than allowing work to get lost in chat. Turn recurring problems and procedures into documentation that makes the next case faster and easier. The longer-term goal is to make support and onboarding increasingly predictable, documented, and independent of senior engineers. Why Join Tricura: Work at the intersection of software engineering, technical operations, and healthcare. Take ownership of two workflows that directly affect customer experience and company growth: onboarding and support. See more of the production system, more customers, and more real-world failure modes than you would on a narrowly scoped feature team. Work closely with experienced engineers and a named mentor from day one. Learn a modern Python and AWS stack in a small, high-autonomy engineering team. Build expertise in a complex clinical domain where the software has a real-world impact on how facilities care for residents. Fully remote 70+ person team across North & South America. High-growth environment with direct exposure to leadership. Mission-driven company improving healthcare through technology. Competitive USD compensation. Unlimited PTO. How to Apply: Please apply by sending your resume in English and a short note on why you're interested directly to Daria Stranadko, Head of People & Talent Development at Tricura: DStranadko@tricurainsurance.io Note: If this role shows as “no longer accepting applications” on LinkedIn, we’re still reviewing candidates. You’re very welcome to apply directly via email.

new_matches.title: Senior Specialist, Employee Relations - EMEA
new_matches.description: About Remote Remote is solving modern organizations’ biggest challenge – navigating global employment compliantly with ease. We make it possible for businesses of all sizes to recruit, pay, and manage international teams. With our core values at heart and future focused work culture, our team works tirelessly on ambitious problems, asynchronously, around the world. You can find Remoters working from 6 different continents (Antarctica left to go!) and all of our positions are fully remote. With Innovation as one of the core values, we have built Automation and AI capabilities into the requirements for every role. We encourage every member of the Remote team to bring their talents, experiences and culture to the table to help us build the best-in-class HR platform. If you are energetic, curious, motivated and ambitious, be part of our world. Apply now and define the future of work! What this job can offer you As a critical extension of our clients’ HR teams, we navigate and advise on the intricate paths of global employment with unmatched speed, expertise, and precision. The vision of the Lifecycle team at Remote is not just about maintaining the gold standard in HR practices; it’s about elevating it, integrating cutting-edge technology solutions, and enriching customer experiences in over 80+ countries. On this team, your work directly influences our ability to sustain and extend our compliance coverage, continuously enhance our customer journeys, and significantly increase our operational capacity. You’re not just part of a team; you’re at the forefront of shaping the future of work, ensuring every interaction is fast, intuitive, and profoundly impactful. Dive into a role where your passion for innovation, commitment to excellence, and drive to make a global difference aligns with our mission to empower organizations worldwide to employ anyone, anywhere — compliantly. The Lifecycle Specialist, Employee Relations & Transitions manages employee exits for Remote's external employees with a focus on legal compliance and providing delightful customer service. Additionally, the specialist provides first-level Employee Relations support, guiding clients through workplace concerns and coordinating appropriate resources when needed. As part of a larger employee Lifecycle team, the Specialist is also expected to contribute to process improvements and initiatives in line with Remote's strategic goals and values. Key Responsibilities Offboarding Manage and resolve end-to-end employee exits across multiple international jurisdictions, prioritizing a superior offboarding experience for Remote's clients and their employees. Provide sound guidance and manage clients' requests on various HR matters, including but not limited to termination, resignation and transfer procedures, employment contracts, and redundancy processes, ensuring legal compliance and best practices. Lead and facilitate meetings with clients and external employees, including but not limited to workforce reduction consultation meetings, administrative hearings, negotiations in separations and settlements, providing guidance on terminations, and delivering termination outcomes. Influence and negotiate positive outcomes in complex terminations, balancing multiple stakeholders with competing interests. Liaise with and coordinate various internal and external stakeholders to ensure compliance in offboarding activities and audits, including but not limited to payroll, legal counsel, government bodies, and trade unions. Draft, tailor and administer all termination and supplementary documents with accuracy and attention to detail, ensuring employee records are maintained with strict adherence to privacy and confidentiality regulations. Process offboarding on Remote's internal HRIS platform, collaborating with various internal stakeholders, such as Customer Success, Legal, Payroll, Benefits, Time and Attendance, amongst other verticals, to ensure all aspects of the employee exit are administered correctly and promptly. Be the subject-matter expert and respond to internal and external queries on all offboarding matters in conjunction with Lifecycle's internal stakeholders. Navigate clients through Remote's Employee Relations resources and guides, helping them understand applicable policies and processes. Conduct preliminary assessment of workplace concerns, identifying key facts and applicable local regulations. Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to ensure appropriate handling of employee relations matters. Support clients in understanding progressive disciplinary approaches and documentation requirements. Monitor ongoing employee relations cases, ensuring timely follow-up and coordination with relevant stakeholders. Actively identify opportunities for and contribute to process improvements, automation, product development and overall customer and employee experience through the offboarding and employee relations processes. Key Requirements and Charactristics Experience as a HR Advisor or HR Business Partner, with generalist HR competencies and exposure across the employee lifecycle. Proven experience with a strong background in managing voluntary and involuntary exits (terminations) with care, sensitivity and legal compliance; and providing comprehensive HR support and guidance on employment laws and regulations, spanning various jurisdictions. Ability to interpret and apply industrial instruments, analyze complex HR issues, undertake research, provide practical solutions and effectively communicate recommendations to clients and internal stakeholders when operating in ambiguous and unfamiliar environments. Basic understanding of employee relations principles, progressive discipline approaches, and workplace investigation fundamentals. Excellent communication, influencing, conflict management, and negotiation skills, with the ability to confidently lead difficult conversations to a positive outcome, often where parties have conflicting interests, maintaining professionalism and strict confidentiality. Business-level (advanced) proficiency in written and spoken English, with additional languages considered a plus. Aptitude and appetite to innovate and optimize processes, continuously identifying and implementing opportunities for automation and championing best practices. Efficiency in operations, with an awareness of the importance of thorough record-keeping and data integrity. Tech-savvy, with the ability to successfully collaborate asynchronously on various tools, and adapt to new and evolving systems. Ability to work autonomously and cohesively in an international team in a fast-paced, asynchronous, remote environment with multiple priorities. Willingness to work flexible hours as needed. Proactive and self-motivated with a strong sense of ownership and accountability. Demonstrates strong automation and AI capabilities and AI fluency. Practicals You'll report to: Manager Employee Lifecycle, Employee Relations & Transitions Team: Lifecycle, Employee Relations & Transitions Location: EMEA Application process Interview with recruiter Take Home Exercise Interview with future manager Interview with team members (no managers present) Interview with Senior Manager Bar Raiser Prior employment verification check Remote's Total Rewards philosophy is to ensure fair, unbiased compensation and fair equity pay along with competitive benefits in all locations in which we operate. We do not agree to or encourage cheap-labor practices and therefore we ensure to pay above in-location rates. We hope to inspire other companies to support global talent-hiring and bring local wealth to developing countries. At first glance our salary bands seem quite wide - here is some context. At Remote we have international operations and a globally distributed workforce. We use geo ranges to consider geographic pay differentials as part of our global compensation strategy to remain competitive in various markets while we hiring globally. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level and location, and our job titles may span more than one career level. The actual base pay for the successful candidate in this role is dependent upon many factors such as location, transferable or job-related skills, work experience, relevant training, business needs, and market demands. The base salary range may be subject to change. At Remote, we foster internal mobility as a key element of our culture of employee growth and development, supported by a compensation philosophy that guarantees pay equity and fairness. Therefore, all compensation changes associated with an internal move will be reviewed by the Total Rewards & People Enablement team on a case by case basis. The annual salary range for this full-time position is $46,500—$104,650 USD Benefits Our full benefits & perks are explained in our handbook at remote.com/r/benefits. As a global company, each country works differently, but some benefits/perks are for all Remoters: work from anywhere flexible paid time off flexible working hours (we are async) 16 weeks paid parental leave budget towards co-working spaces, learning and wellness (including gym memberships) mental health support services stock options home office budget & IT equipment How You’ll Plan Your Day (and Life) We work async at Remote which means you can plan your schedule around your life (and not around meetings). Read more at remote.com/async. You will be empowered to take ownership and be proactive. When in doubt you will default to action instead of waiting. Your life-work balance is important and you will be encouraged to put yourself and your family first, and fit work around your needs. If that sounds like something you want, apply now! How To Apply Please fill out the form below and upload your CV with a PDF format. We kindly ask you to submit your application and CV in English, as this is the standardised language we use here at Remote. If you don’t have an up to date CV but you are still interested in talking to us, please feel free to add a copy of your LinkedIn profile instead. Not only do we encourage folks from all ethnic groups, genders, sexuality, age, abilities, disability status and any other under-represented group to apply, but we prioritize a sense of belonging. We have 4 ERGs (Women, Disability, Queer, Minorities in Tech) who meet regularly with the People team. During your interviews and beyond, we ask & encourage anybody who needs an accommodation to request one from their recruiter. We will ask you to voluntarily tell us your pronouns at interview stage, and you will have the option to answer our anonymous demographic questionnaire when you apply below. As an equal employment opportunity employer it’s important to us that our workforce reflects people of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences and this data will help us to stay accountable. We thank you for providing this data, if you chose to. At Remote, we embrace AI as a valuable tool while prioritizing human creativity and authenticity. We look forward to meeting candidates who balance innovation with genuine expertise and experience. To learn more about Remote's AI guidelines check see here. Please note we accept applications on an ongoing basis.

Create the planning, preparation, and structure that allow the SVP to focus on the most important business priorities. Manage a complex international calendar, travel arrangements, meeting preparation, correspondence, expenses, and other executive-level administration. Establish strong relationships across the leadership and EA community, acting as a reliable connection point between the SVP and key stakeholders. Anticipate upcoming meetings and decisions, ensuring that the right stakeholders are engaged and the necessary information is available in advance. Coordinate executive meetings, leadership events, and off-sites, ensuring a seamless experience from planning through execution. Contribute to an inclusive and collaborative EA community through knowledge sharing, coordination, and peer support. Support selected communications or cross-functional initiatives based on business needs and your individual strengths. What Will Help You Succeed Significant experience supporting a senior executive in a complex, international organization. Exceptional planning, organization, and prioritization skills. A proactive mindset and the ability to anticipate needs before they become urgent. Strong stakeholder-management skills and the confidence to work with senior leaders across functions and geographies. Excellent written and verbal communication. Sound judgment and the ability to handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion. A collaborative, service-oriented approach that builds trust and makes it easy for others to engage. High attention to detail and a strong commitment to following established policies and processes. Adaptability and composure when priorities change. Confidence using Microsoft Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and related collaboration tools. Availability for occasional domestic and international travel. Helpful, But Not Essential Previous experience supporting a C-suite executive or company president. Experience coordinating leadership events, off-sites, or executive programs. Interest or experience in internal communications, special projects, or EA-community development. Familiarity with continuous-improvement principles. Formal project-management experience. What Makes This Role Different This is more than a role that manages an executive’s schedule. It is an opportunity to build a close partnership with a senior leader, work across an international stakeholder community, and help improve the flow of information and collaboration across Product Quality & Innovation. The successful candidate will have the freedom to bring ideas, improve how work gets done, and expand their contribution over time through areas such as leadership events, communications, special initiatives, or EA-community development. new_matches.title: Junior Support Engineer
new_matches.description: Junior Support Engineer 📍 Remote (Latin America-based; English-fluent) About the Company: Tricura Insurance Group is a next-generation, tech-enabled insurance and risk management company transforming how healthcare organizations protect, manage, and grow their operations. We're a global, remote-first team with headquarters in New York, reshaping the future of healthcare insurance. By combining deep industry expertise with modern technology, we deliver smarter, faster, and more transparent insurance solutions across the continuum of care. If you're motivated by impact, innovation, and purpose, you'll find your place here. About the Role: Tricura builds software for long-term-care and senior-living operators, turning clinical data from facility EHR systems into real-time alerts, compliance checks, and analytics. Our customers run dozens of facilities each, and the data behind every alert arrives through integrations we build and operate ourselves. Two things gate how fast we grow: how quickly we bring a new customer's data online, and how quickly we answer when something looks wrong. Both currently land on senior engineers as interrupts. This role exists to own those workflows properly and give the engineering team room to focus on deeper product and technical work. You're the first engineer on every incoming issue and every new customer connection. You diagnose before you escalate, run the onboarding sequence end to end, and write down how all of it works. Most customer issues reach engineering through our Customer Success team. You'll work closely with CS to understand what the customer is experiencing, investigate what is actually happening, and provide a clear technical answer or next step. CS owns the customer communication; you own the technical investigation, resolution, and handoff. This is an entry-level engineering role with a strong technical operations and support component. Some days you'll investigate an interesting production issue; other days you'll work through a detailed onboarding checklist or follow up on a missing access credential. The ability to approach both with the same level of care is central to succeeding in the role. What You'll Do: First response and triage. Reproduce incoming issues and classify them: genuine defect, expected behavior, data or config problem, or a question that needs a clear explanation rather than a fix. Resolve what you can, escalate well. Own straightforward issues to closure. When something needs a senior engineer, hand it over with the reproduction, the logs and queries, and the diagnosis already narrowed — never a forwarded complaint. Use good judgment about when to stop investigating. Your job is to identify the problem, gather enough evidence to establish what is happening, and escalate deeper issues effectively — not to disappear down a multi-day engineering rabbit hole. Work closely with Customer Success. CS is typically the channel through which customer feedback reaches engineering. You'll turn incomplete or sometimes ambiguous reports into actionable technical investigations and give CS the information they need to respond back to the customer. Run customer onboarding operations. Drive new orgs and facilities from intake through provisioning: the access and credential sequence with each customer's EHR vendor, configuration in our platform, and verification that data is actually flowing before anyone calls it live. Manage the onboarding checklist end to end. Work through the required technical steps, identify what information or access is missing or incorrect, and coordinate the follow-up needed to get onboarding unstuck. Keep the pipeline visible. Every in-flight onboarding tracked with its real blocker and its real owner, in the issue tracker rather than in chat history. Investigate data and configuration issues. Use the available platform data, queries, logs, and source-system information to determine whether an issue originates in incoming data, configuration, or the application itself. Follow established technical procedures. Existing onboarding and support workflows are documented and intentionally step-by-step. You'll learn them, execute them consistently, and gradually become able to run them independently. Write the playbooks. Every recurring procedure becomes a runbook: the steps, the failure modes, what to check, when to escalate. This is the lasting output of the role, not an afterthought. Turn tribal knowledge into documentation. When you learn how to solve a recurring problem that currently lives in someone's head, capture it so another person can follow the same process without needing to ask. Follow QA-quality bug reporting standards. Reproduction steps, evidence, and issue descriptions should be consistent with the standards used by the QA team so that engineering receives actionable bugs. Ship small fixes. Config corrections, data-quality queries, verification scripts, well-scoped bug fixes, reviewed like any other change. Who We're Looking For: 0–2 years of professional software experience , and a strong Computer Science / Engineering degree with real project work . We'll teach the domain; we won't teach how to think about a problem. Python and SQL. Read an unfamiliar Python codebase and follow what it does. Write SQL well enough to answer "is this customer's data actually correct?" unaided. Systematic debugging. Hypothesis, test, and the difference between a symptom and a cause. Comfortable saying "I reproduced it and here's why it happens." Strong signal-vs-noise judgment. You can distinguish a genuine defect from expected behavior, a configuration issue, bad or missing data, or a misunderstanding — and you don't automatically turn every customer complaint into a bug. Professional English fluency. Most of the job is written — triage notes, escalations, runbooks, status updates read by US-based colleagues. Clear communication. You can take a messy or incomplete problem statement and turn it into a structured explanation of what you know, what you tested, what remains unclear, and what needs to happen next. Comfort with ambiguity and process work. Some days are a genuinely interesting bug. Some days are chasing an access request through three parties. The role needs someone who treats the second with the same care as the first. Comfort learning from others. This is a junior role in a technically complex environment. You won't know everything, and that's expected. We value someone who can say "I don't know yet," ask a good question, and then learn from the answer. Attention to detail. Small differences in credentials, facility information, configuration, or incoming data can determine whether an onboarding succeeds. Ownership and follow-through. You don't need someone constantly reminding you which onboarding step is blocked or which investigation still needs an answer. Availability to work from 9 am to 6 pm EST . Strong Plus: Internship, university, side-project, open-source, or other hands-on experience where you've actually built or debugged software. Experience working with technical support, QA, incident triage, NOC, or production operations. Experience investigating issues in software you didn't originally build. Experience working with databases and using SQL to validate whether data is correct. Experience creating technical documentation, runbooks, READMEs, troubleshooting guides, or similar materials that other people could follow. Experience working with healthcare, long-term care, senior living, EHR systems, or other regulated environments with real privacy constraints. Experience with AWS, Airflow-style or similar workflow orchestration, cloud data platforms, warehouses, or related infrastructure. What Success Looks Like: In the first months, you'll learn the onboarding and support workflows, become comfortable navigating the relevant systems, and begin handling routine cases with guidance. Over time, you'll be able to independently: Triage incoming issues and quickly determine whether they are bugs, configuration/data issues, expected behavior, or misunderstandings. Reproduce and document problems clearly enough for engineering or QA to act on them. Resolve routine support and configuration issues without pulling senior engineers into the work. Run customer onboarding through the required technical steps and identify exactly what is blocking progress. Keep onboarding status and ownership visible rather than allowing work to get lost in chat. Turn recurring problems and procedures into documentation that makes the next case faster and easier. The longer-term goal is to make support and onboarding increasingly predictable, documented, and independent of senior engineers. Why Join Tricura: Work at the intersection of software engineering, technical operations, and healthcare. Take ownership of two workflows that directly affect customer experience and company growth: onboarding and support. See more of the production system, more customers, and more real-world failure modes than you would on a narrowly scoped feature team. Work closely with experienced engineers and a named mentor from day one. Learn a modern Python and AWS stack in a small, high-autonomy engineering team. Build expertise in a complex clinical domain where the software has a real-world impact on how facilities care for residents. Fully remote 70+ person team across North & South America. High-growth environment with direct exposure to leadership. Mission-driven company improving healthcare through technology. Competitive USD compensation. Unlimited PTO. How to Apply: Please apply by sending your resume in English and a short note on why you're interested directly to Daria Stranadko, Head of People & Talent Development at Tricura: DStranadko@tricurainsurance.io Note: If this role shows as “no longer accepting applications” on LinkedIn, we’re still reviewing candidates. You’re very welcome to apply directly via email.
